threats_not_stated_by_authors: Only Mamba-2.8b and Pythia-2.8b are tested; no evidence that findings transfer to Gemma 4 E2B, KV-shared layers 15-34, or per-layer embeddings.
Subject-swapping activation patching may entangle entity recognition, relation extraction, and factual recall, especially for multi-token subjects.
ROME evaluation uses the first 2000 COUNTERFACT examples and a limited set of relations, so edit success may not generalize across broader factual distributions.
LRE hyperparameters are selected by grid search, which may overfit the small n=5 sample and inflate faithfulness estimates.
Mean-ablation attention knockout is coarse and can affect multiple token paths, so it cannot isolate specific token-to-token information flow.
The paper does not test CPU-only feasibility or the cost of Jacobian/activation-patching sweeps for larger models such as Gemma 4 E2B.
No logit-lens or induction-head analysis is performed, so direct relevance to those lab tools is unverified.
data.relevance_to_lab: The paper's activation-patching, path-blocking, ROME, LRE, and attention-knockout protocols are directly analogous to the lab's factual-recall tracing and activation patching on Gemma 4 E2B; however, it studies Mamba-2.8b/Pythia-2.8b, not KV-shared layers 15-34 or per-layer embeddings, so transfer to Gemma internals and CPU constraints must be validated.

data.title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in Mamba
data.research_question: Can factual recall in Mamba be localized and edited like factual recall in autoregressive transformer LMs, and which transformer interpretability methods transfer to the Mamba architecture?

models_and_data.item: Mamba-2.8b, the primary Mamba recurrent state-space language model
models_and_data.quote: In this work we conduct our experiments on Mamba-2.8b, the largest available LM in Mamba family, and for comparison we conduct the same experiments on the similarly sized Pythia-2.8b (Biderman et al., 2023) autoregressive transformer LM.

models_and_data.item: Pythia-2.8b, the similarly sized autoregressive transformer comparison model
models_and_data.quote: and for comparison we conduct the same experiments on the similarly sized Pythia-2.8b (Biderman et al., 2023) autoregressive transformer LM.

models_and_data.item: COUNTERFACT: 20K counterfactual edit examples; the first 2000 records were used for the module-layer sweep
models_and_data.quote: C OUNTER FACT contains 20K counterfactual examples in the form (s, r, o → o ∗ )

models_and_data.item: RELATIONS: 47 relations total, 26 factual relations used; six factual relations used for the intervention experiments
models_and_data.quote: In the scope of this paper, we only utilize the 26 factual relations from this dataset.

models_and_data.item: WikiText-103: 10,000-token sample used to estimate mean a-states for mean ablation
models_and_data.quote: where E a(ℓ) is the mean of a(ℓ) states collected with 10,000 tokens from WikiText-103 by Merity et al. (2016).

protocol.step: For each known fact, run a clean pass, a subject-swapped corrupted pass, and a patched pass that restores a selected clean state into its corresponding corrupted-run position.
protocol.quote: A state from the clean run G is patched into its corresponding position in the corrupted run G ∗ .

protocol.step: Repeat residual-state restoration while severing selected selective-SSM, gate, or output contribution paths to measure path-specific mediation.
protocol.quote: The same experiment is replicated to understand the contributions of gi and oi states.

protocol.step: Sweep ROME rank-one edits over the Wa, Wg, and Wo projection matrices at every Mamba layer.
protocol.quote: We apply ROME on the three different projection matrices of Mamba: Wa which affects only the Conv + SSM path, Wg which affects only the gating path, and Wo , the final output of the MambaBlock

protocol.step: Evaluate edits using the first 2000 COUNTERFACT examples and the original ROME evaluation matrices.
protocol.quote: We select the first 2000 examples from this dataset for our module-layer sweep.

protocol.step: Grid-search the LRE hyperparameters β, ρ and the layer from which the enriched subject representation is extracted.
protocol.quote: We find the hyperparameters β, ρ and the layer ℓ (where to extract the enriched s from) using grid search.

protocol.step: Measure LRE faithfulness using n = 5 samples across all 26 factual relations.
protocol.quote: We plot the faithfulness of L RE with n = 5 samples on Figure 7.

protocol.step: Mean-ablate a states to block source-token propagation to all future tokens, using 10-layer windows over 700 facts from six relations.
protocol.quote: However, it is possible to block the propagation of information from the kth token to all the future tokens via Conv + SSM operation by mean-ablation.

protocol.step: Run parallel ROME experiments on the similarly sized Pythia-2.8b model for architectural comparison.
protocol.quote: We plot ROME performance for a similar sized Pythia model on Figure 6b for comparison.

metrics.name: Indirect Effect (IE)
metrics.definition: Normalized change in correct-answer probability under state restoration, divided by the clean-versus-corrupted probability gap.
metrics.quote: Let p(o ), p∗ (o ), and p∗ [← hi ](o ) denote the probability assigned to the correct answer o in G, G ∗ , and G ∗ [← hi ] respectively. To measure the contribution of hi (ℓ) we define its indirect effect (IE) as:

metrics.name: Efficacy (ES)
metrics.definition: Fraction of edited examples for which the post-edit model assigns greater probability to the counterfactual object than to the original object.
metrics.quote: Efficacy (ES): For an edit request (s, r, o → o ∗ ), we say the edit is effective if, post-edit, the LM assigns p(o ∗ ) > p(o ) in response to the prompt x = (s, r ).

metrics.name: Generalization (PS)
metrics.definition: Whether an edit remains effective across paraphrases of the original subject-relation prompt.
metrics.quote: Generalization (PS): A successful edit should be persistent across different paraphrases of (s, r ).

metrics.name: Specificity (NS)
metrics.definition: Whether the edit leaves nearby factual subject-relation mappings unchanged.
metrics.quote: Specificity (NS): Finally, the edit should be specific to Pr (s) and should not additionally change the mapping of some nearby subject sn to o ∗ .

metrics.name: ROME Score (S)
metrics.definition: Harmonic mean of the efficacy, generalization, and specificity scores.
metrics.quote: The final score (S) in the ROME evaluation suite is the harmonic mean of three different scores:

metrics.name: LRE Faithfulness
metrics.definition: Portion of facts correctly retrieved when the model's factual computation is replaced by the affine LRE approximation.
metrics.quote: The metric faithfulness represents the portion of facts (s, r, o ) that can be correctly retrieved if the LM computation F (s, r ) is replaced with L RE (s), a simple affine transformation.

metrics.name: LRE Causality
metrics.definition: Counterfactual test of whether an LRE-consistent subject perturbation moves model output toward a specified alternative object.
metrics.quote: Besides faithfulness Hernandez et al. (2023) introduced another metric causality to measure the performance of L RE.

metrics.name: Relative Change in p(o)
metrics.definition: Relative change in correct-answer probability after blocking Conv + SSM information propagation with mean ablation.
metrics.quote: The effect of blocking out Conv + SSM information flow for certain layer-token (ℓ − k) positions is measured as the relative change in p(o )

key_results.claim: Activation patching reveals localized factual-recall effects at the last subject token and specific layer ranges in Mamba, resembling autoregressive transformer LMs.
key_results.quote: with activation patching we have found that, similar to autoregressive transformer LMs, Mamba shows signs of localization at the last subject token and at specific layer ranges while recalling a fact.

key_results.claim: Residual-state IE is concentrated at the subject-last token through layer 46, while the later-site IE jumps to 1.0 after layer 46.
key_results.numbers: up to layer 46; jumps to 1.0 after layer 46
key_results.quote: hi up to layer 46 only show strong IE at the subject last token position and have negligible impact after that. Whereas IE of hi jumps to 1.0 after layer 46.

key_results.claim: At the subject-last early site, Conv + SSM and Wg mediate strongly but Wo has the largest role; Wo is also the strongest mediator at the late site.
key_results.quote: both the Conv + SSM and Wg have a strong role, but Wo plays an even larger role than either. Yet the strongest mediator at the late site is also Wo .

key_results.claim: ROME can achieve high scores over a range of early-to-middle layers by editing Wa, Wg, or Wo.
key_results.quote: ROME can achieve high scores (S) for a range of early to middle layers by modifying any one of the projection matrices Wa , Wg , or Wo , matching observations made by Hase et al. (2024) regarding transformer LMs.

key_results.claim: The best ROME performance is empirically obtained by editing Wo.
key_results.quote: Our experiments further show that the best performance for ROME is empirically achieved by modifying Wo .

key_results.claim: A linear LRE exceeds 50% faithfulness for only 10 of 26 factual relations in Mamba, compared with 11 relations in Pythia-2.8b.
key_results.numbers: 10 out of 26; more than 50%; Pythia-2.8b: > 50% for 11 factual relations
key_results.quote: Figure 7 shows that only for 10 out of 26 factual relations can a linear L RE achieve more than 50% faithfulness. For comparison, in the same sized Pythia-2.8b L RE achives > 50% faithfulness for 11 factual relations (see Appendix E).

key_results.claim: Blocking non-subject Conv + SSM information flow in early-middle layers can reduce correct-answer probability substantially.
key_results.quote: The purple lines show that blocking out non-subject information flow in early middle layers can bring down p(o ) by up to 50%.

key_results.claim: Subject information is propagated to later tokens through Conv + SSM paths in layers 43-48.
key_results.quote: However, the valley at layers 43-48 suggest that Mamba uses Conv + SSM paths in those layers to propagate critical information from the subject to later tokens.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The empirical study covers only one Mamba model and one similarly sized transformer comparator.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Although our experiments have been limited to Mamba-2.8b, the largest available LM of that family, and comparisons to the similarly-sized transformer Pythia-2.8b, the methods we have introduced are general, and can be used to analyze to any state-space model.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Edge-specific information-flow knockout is difficult because of the interaction between convolution, its nonlinearity, and the selective SSM.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The use of Conv with a non-linearity in conjunction with selective-SSM make it challenging to remove the information retained in the qth token from the kth token (see Appendix B for details).

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The convolutional receptive field allows information to leak across token edges even after a putative edge-specific intervention.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Note that, since ck is a convolved state with a receptive field of size 4 in Mamba-2.8b, the states ck+1 , ck+2 , and ck+3 also retain information from ak .

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The implemented mean-ablation intervention is less surgical than cutting a specific information-flow edge.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: We recognize that this intervention may not be as surgical as cutting a specific edge.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The intervention cannot isolate a unique causal role for the prompt-last token.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: However, unlike Geva et al. (2023), we cannot make strong claims about the unique role of the final token position (prompt-last) with this experiment.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: LRE was evaluated only on factual relations rather than all relation types in RELATIONS.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: We only calculate L RE for the factual relations in the R ELATIONS dataset.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Some transformer-specific interpretation methods do not transfer to Mamba easily because of architectural constraints.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: We also discuss mismatches—that is, interpretation methods (such as path-dependent attention patching) that do not transfer to Mamba as easily due to architectural constraints.

threats_not_stated_by_authors: Mamba-2.8b findings may not transfer to Gemma 4 E2B because Conv + SSM, attention, parameterization, scale, tokenizer, and training differ despite the shared autoregressive objective.
In Gemma's KV-shared layers 15-34, restoring one per-layer embedding may influence several downstream layers, making attribution to an individual layer non-identifiable.
CPU execution and possible numerical or precision differences could alter activation magnitudes and the normalization-sensitive IE denominator.
Subject-swap counterfactuals require a different answer and may remain out-of-distribution or semantically confounded, making clean-corrupted probability gaps unstable.
Patching and mean-ablation may impair generic token processing, so a reduction in p(o) need not specifically represent factual-association mediation.
ROME uses the first 2000 COUNTERFACT records and patching uses 400 examples from six relations, so results may depend on dataset ordering and relation coverage.
Per-relation LRE grid search with n = 5 can overfit the sampled facts, and high faithfulness alone does not establish a causal mechanism.
Subject-last effects may shift with tokenization or prompt length, and Mamba-derived layer windows may not correspond to Gemma's layer indexing.
data.relevance_to_lab: Directly relevant as a methodological template for Gemma 4 E2B: apply activation patching to per-layer embeddings, contrast subject-last and prompt-last positions, and test whether layers 15-34 show localized causal effects under KV sharing. The paper supplies testable baselines involving early-middle subject-token localization, later prompt-token effects, path attribution, relation-wise linearity, and rank-one edits. These can be combined with logit lens, induction-head analysis, and factual-recall tracing on CPU. Its Conv + SSM knockout caveat is especially relevant because Gemma requires edge-specific interventions to be redesigned around attention and KV paths. The paper's layer ranges and Mamba component roles should be treated as hypotheses rather than directly transferable findings for Gemma.
